title: Planning for Medical Emergencies
cross_references: Medical Incident Report, ICS 206 WF, on page 120

nodes.text: What are we going to do if someone gets hurt?

evidence.source_text: 1. What are we going to do if someone gets hurt?

nodes.text: Consider if there are personnel on your crew/division/fire that can provide medical support

evidence.source_text: • Are there personnel on your crew/division/fire that can provide medical support?

nodes.text: Consider what type of equipment is available to treat and transport injured personnel

evidence.source_text: • What type of equipment is available to treat and transport injured personnel?

nodes.text: How will we get them out of here?

evidence.source_text: 2. How will we get them out of here?

nodes.text: Consider if you could get an injured firefighter to a road or helispot

evidence.source_text: • Could you get an injured firefighter to a road or helispot?

nodes.text: Consider how many personnel and what kind of equipment would you need to get an injured firefighter out

evidence.source_text: • How many personnel and what kind of equipment would you need to get an injured firefighter out?

nodes.text: How long will it take to get them to a hospital?

evidence.source_text: 3. How long will it take to get them to a hospital?

nodes.text: Consider where is the closest hospital
Consider if you will use air or ground transportation

evidence.source_text: • Will you use air or ground transportation?

nodes.text: Consider if conditions could change and affect the transportation timeline

evidence.source_text: • Could conditions change and affect the transportation timeline?

nodes.text: Consider smoke/clouds/nightfall, fire behavior, mechanical failures
Base all operational activities on answers to these questions

evidence.source_text: All operational activities should be based on answers to these questions.

nodes.text: If answers are insufficient, stop, reassess, and consider alternate strategies and tactics
